summary: The paper compares four freestanding Ti3C2Tx film electrodes: large-flake pristine and H2SO4-etched films (L-pristine and L-etched), and probe-sonicated small-flake pristine and etched films (S-pristine and S-etched). All MXene originated from HF/HCl etching of Ti3AlC2 followed by LiCl delamination; etched samples underwent concentrated H2SO4 oxidation, while S samples additionally underwent probe sonication. S-etched is the headline material, reaching 327 F g−1 and approximately 1200 F cm−3 at 5 mV s−1 for a 1.1 µm, 0.4 mg cm−2 film; its highest reported areal capacitance was 3.2 F cm−2 at 48 µm and 12 mg cm−2. Absolute XRD d-spacings, BET surface areas, porosity, and most numerical capacitances for the three comparison films were not printed in the supplied paper text.
